# Agentic AI for Serious Engineers

> A practical field guide to building reliable, evaluable, and production-grade agent systems. Companion site to the book by Sunil Prakash.

The book is available on Amazon: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0GVG6848F
The site is at: https://agenticlab.sunilprakash.com/

## Editorial structure

The publication is organised as a layered editorial system. The book is the canonical reference. Four ongoing streams sit alongside it: Field Notes, Signal, Recipes, and Labs. Evidence, Patterns, and Projects are reference material.

- The book: 13 chapters across four parts, plus 5 foundation pre-reads
- Field Notes: short observations from inside the work
- Signal: commentary on the discourse around agent engineering (papers, tools, marketplaces, vendor claims)
- Recipes: buildable-in-an-afternoon walkthroughs with verified code
- Labs: empirical lab reports with measured comparisons
- Evidence: measured eval data backing claims made in the book
- Patterns: reusable architectural patterns referenced across the work
- Projects: case-study teardowns of reference agent systems

## The book

Foundations (zero-to-agent pre-reads):
- [How LLMs Actually Work](https://agenticlab.sunilprakash.com/book/00a-how-llms-work/): Engineer's mental model — APIs, tokens, context, hallucination
- [From API Calls to Tool Use](https://agenticlab.sunilprakash.com/book/00b-api-to-tools/): Function calling, schema validation, giving the model hands
- [Your First Agent, No Framework](https://agenticlab.sunilprakash.com/book/00c-first-agent/): Build a complete agent in 100 lines
- [The Same Agent, With a Framework](https://agenticlab.sunilprakash.com/book/00d-frameworks/): ADK and LangChain side by side
- [Connecting Your Agent to MCP](https://agenticlab.sunilprakash.com/book/00e-connecting-to-mcp/): Build an MCP server, connect to real tools

Part I — Building:
- [Ch 1: What "Agentic" Actually Means](https://agenticlab.sunilprakash.com/book/01-what-agentic-means/): Precise definitions, decision map
- [Ch 2: Tools, Context, and the Agent Loop](https://agenticlab.sunilprakash.com/book/02-tools-context-agent-loop/): Tool registry, context pipeline
- [Ch 3: Workflow First, Agent Second](https://agenticlab.sunilprakash.com/book/03-workflow-first-agent-second/): Same task two ways
- [Ch 4: Multi-Agent Systems Without Theater](https://agenticlab.sunilprakash.com/book/04-multi-agent-without-theater/): Coordination, MCP, A2A, AIP

Part II — Judging:
- [Ch 5: Human-in-the-Loop as Architecture](https://agenticlab.sunilprakash.com/book/05-human-in-the-loop/): Approval gates, escalation, audit
- [Ch 6: Evaluating and Hardening Agents](https://agenticlab.sunilprakash.com/book/06-evaluating-and-hardening/): Eval, tracing, reliability, security
- [Ch 7: When Not to Use Agents](https://agenticlab.sunilprakash.com/book/07-when-not-to-use-agents/): Building engineering judgment

Part III — Operating:
- [Ch 8: Metacognition and Self-Reflection](https://agenticlab.sunilprakash.com/book/08-metacognition/): Loop detection, strategy switching
- [Ch 9: Deploying and Scaling Agent Systems](https://agenticlab.sunilprakash.com/book/09-deployment/): Durable execution, observability
- [Ch 10: Agent Governance and Auditability](https://agenticlab.sunilprakash.com/book/10-governance/): Decision traces, compliance
- [Ch 11: Security Deep Dive](https://agenticlab.sunilprakash.com/book/11-security/): The Lethal Trifecta, defense in depth

Part IV — Advanced Patterns:
- [Ch 12: Memory Management](https://agenticlab.sunilprakash.com/book/12-memory-management/): Session, long-term, shared memory
- [Ch 13: Agent Protocols in Production](https://agenticlab.sunilprakash.com/book/13-agent-protocols-in-production/): Enterprise MCP, A2A at scale, AIP delegation

## Field Notes

Twice-weekly observations on building agents that survive contact with reality.

- [FN-001: The multi-agent papers nobody is citing](https://agenticlab.sunilprakash.com/field-notes/001-multi-agent-papers-nobody-cites/): Three 2025 studies put multi-agent failure rates between 41 and 86.7 percent
- [FN-002: Your eval rubric needs failure buckets, not just scores](https://agenticlab.sunilprakash.com/field-notes/002-eval-rubric-failure-buckets/): Two agents can score identically on a benchmark and fail differently in production

Index: https://agenticlab.sunilprakash.com/field-notes/

## Signal

Commentary on the discourse around agent engineering. What to keep, what to skip.

- [SG-001: The skills.md discourse is sharpening the wrong knife](https://agenticlab.sunilprakash.com/signal/001-skills-md-wrong-knife/): The 1% context-window description budget is the actual constraint, not body size

Index: https://agenticlab.sunilprakash.com/signal/

## Voice and audience

This publication is written for backend engineers, platform engineers, staff+ engineers, software architects, and technical leads building AI systems for production use. The book and the ongoing streams favor opinionated engineering judgment, named failure modes, working code, restraint over breadth, and evidence over hype.

Assumed baseline: APIs, Python, software architecture, services, testing, databases, production experience. Not assumed: transformers, embeddings, agent orchestration, AI evaluation. These are taught in the book.

## Author

Sunil Prakash — engineering leader and researcher focused on enterprise AI systems, agent identity protocols, and production agent architecture. Author profile: https://sunilprakash.com
